# 616: Kvalitet vs. disrupsjon – hva kjennetegner fremtidens vinnere?

**Feed**: pengepodden-no  
**Published**: 2026-10-22  
**Market Sentiment**: Positive

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

This Norwegian Pengepodden episode is a Nordnet Live panel. It compares quality investing, represented by Bernt Berg Nilsen of Stolt Explorer, with disruption investing, represented by Leo Rundgren Olsen of DNB Disruptive Opportunities. Berg Nilsen backs steadily profitable compounders with high return on capital and holding companies trading at a discount to NAV, such as Aker and Investor. Olsen backs companies early on an S-curve of adoption and names AI infrastructure, robotics and cybersecurity. Both managers own Nvidia and expect it to outgrow Apple. Both expect the S&P 500 to be higher in 12 months, while Berg Nilsen thinks an AI crash within two years is possible.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 NVDA — Nvidia | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 80%

Both funds own it. Leo expects it to stay top 5 for 5-10 years; Bernt says it has become cheap. Both expect it to be bigger than Apple in 5 years.

#### Reasoning

Both the quality manager and the disruption manager own Nvidia. Leo says it invests across the whole ecosystem (simulation, world models, networking), not just chips. Bernt notes it now looks cheap on valuation, so it fits both growth and value. Both answered yes that it will be bigger than Apple in five years.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the chip business matures without new S-curves (world models, infrastructure)
- if an AI crash hits the market
- if its valuation re-expands without matching earnings

> *"Og det gjør at vi tror at det kommer til å være et selskap som fortsatt kommer til å være topp 5 de neste 5-10 årene."*

---

### 🟢 AKER — Aker | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Stolt Explorer's largest holding. The disruption manager wishes his fund owned it. Long record of NAV growth.

#### Reasoning

Bernt's quality-holding-company test is NAV growth over time, low management cost relative to NAV, and ideally buying at a discount to NAV. Aker has compounded NAV about 13-14% a year plus dividends over 20 years, even faster recently, and has grown into the fund's top weight. Leo named it as the stock he would most like to own in the current market.

#### Sell Triggers

- if NAV growth slows below market returns
- if the discount to NAV closes or turns into a premium
- if capital allocation weakens

> *"det blir jo feil å ikke si noe annet enn aker, hvertfall i det markedet vi er i nå"*

---

### 🟢 CRWD — CrowdStrike | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 65%

DNB Disruptive holds it and it is up about 100% this year. Leo sees a structural shift to constant cyber protection.

#### Reasoning

Leo admits it looks expensive on historical numbers. He argues cybersecurity has changed from rare all-hands responses after a hack to constant attacks, so customers must pay more and pay continuously. Bernt agrees it is the right theme and the right company, and regrets passing on it because of the price.

#### Sell Triggers

- if security spending growth slows
- if valuation runs ahead of fundamentals
- if competitors take share

> *"Nå skjer det konstant, så du er nødt til å betale mye mer, og er villig til å gjøre det og beskytte deg konstant"*

---

### 🟡 INVE-B — Investor | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Bernt's example of a quality holding company, with about 13-14% annual NAV growth plus dividends over 20 years.

#### Reasoning

Bernt names Investor alongside Aker as the model for his core 'quality' bucket. Both have long records of NAV compounding well above the stock market's 8-9% a year. He does not say explicitly that Stolt Explorer owns it, so conviction is lower.

#### Sell Triggers

- if NAV growth falls below market return
- if the stock trades at a large premium to NAV

> *"så har Aker og Investor avkastet altså vokst sin veldig sterkte egenskapital med hensyn til 13 og 14 prosent pluss utbytter i året"*

---

### 🟡 ASML — ASML | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Stolt Explorer holding bought for its monopoly position, which then benefited from the capex order boom.

#### Reasoning

This is an example of the fund's 'start equal-weight and let winners grow' method. The thesis was the long-standing monopoly, not a forecast of the boom.

#### Sell Triggers

- if its monopoly position erodes
- if the semiconductor capex cycle reverses

> *"men vi visste at ASML var en monopolist og hadde vært i mange år"*

---

### 🟠 TSLA — Tesla | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 45%

Leo argues the market overprices its risk compared with Volkswagen, and that it is disrupting itself with self-driving and robots.

#### Reasoning

Leo uses Tesla to show that the market misprices beta: Tesla takes market share and is a better company than Volkswagen, yet is treated as riskier. He likes its ability to replace its own car business with autonomy and robotics. He never says the fund owns it.

#### Sell Triggers

- if self-driving and robotics fail to scale
- if it keeps losing car market share

> *"Er Tesla mye høyere risiko enn Volkswagen når de tar maksjøndeler og er et bedre selskap?"*

---

### ⛔ AAPL — Apple | **AVOID** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 45%

DNB Disruptive does not own it because Leo is unsure Apple can build a new S-curve. Both managers expect Nvidia to be bigger in 5 years.

#### Reasoning

Apple has a history of disrupting itself (the iPhone replaced the iPod), but Leo doubts it can find its next growth curve, so the fund stays out. Both managers expect Nvidia to overtake Apple in size within five years.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Apple launches a credible new S-curve product (this would turn the view positive)

> *"nå er jeg litt usikker på om de klarer å etablere en ny S-kurve, derfor har ikke vi det i porteføljen"*

---

### 🟠 PROT — Protector Forsikring | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Bernt's biggest 'mistake of omission': he passed because it looked expensive, and it has run strongly for the past four years.

#### Reasoning

Bernt names Protector as his biggest miss. It was within his circle of competence, but he passed on price and the stock has risen strongly for four years. He does not say whether he would buy it now.

#### Sell Triggers

- if insurance profitability or combined ratios deteriorate
- if valuation stays stretched

> *"jeg burde ha fått ut en protektor"*

---
